facts.fact: Nielsen's 2025 State of Play report, as cited by AdWave, says the average American adult spends 4 hours and 59 minutes per day watching TV content.
facts.quote: the average American adult spends 4 hours and 59 minutes per day watching TV content

facts.fact: Nielsen's 2025 State of Play report, as cited by AdWave, says the average American adult spends 4 hours and 37 minutes per day on their smartphone.
facts.quote: 4 hours and 37 minutes on their smartphone

facts.fact: A Video Advertising Bureau study (2024), cited by AdWave, found campaigns using TV plus digital together saw a 23% increase in ad recall compared to either channel alone.
facts.quote: campaigns using TV plus digital together saw a 23% increase in ad recall compared to either channel alone (VAB, 2024)

facts.fact: AdImpact reported that US political digital ad spending reached $3.46 billion in 2024, as cited by AdWave.
facts.quote: AdImpact reported that political digital ad spending reached $3.46 billion in 2024

facts.fact: AdWave's suggested sequential plan starts with a TV ad in Days 1-3 that introduces the candidate and core message, followed by mobile ads in Days 4-7 and Days 8-14.
facts.quote: **Day 1-3:** TV ad introduces the candidate and core message

facts.fact: AdWave gives an example sequential targeting rule: after a household sees a TV ad, serve a mobile ad to that household within 48 hours.
facts.quote: After this household sees my TV ad, serve this mobile ad in the next 48 hours.

facts.fact: AdWave defines the heavy streamer voter segment as ages 18-34, who watch most TV content on streaming platforms and are heavy mobile users.
facts.quote: Heavy streamers (ages 18-34):** These voters watch most of their TV content on streaming platforms

facts.fact: For a statewide race (governor, senate), the recommended budget split is 55-65% CTV/streaming TV and 35-45% mobile/digital.
facts.quote: **Statewide race (governor, senate):** * CTV/Streaming TV: 55-65% * Mobile/Digital: 35-45%

facts.fact: For a congressional district race, the recommended budget split is 45-55% CTV/streaming TV and 45-55% mobile/digital.
facts.quote: **Congressional district:** * CTV/Streaming TV: 45-55% * Mobile/Digital: 45-55%

facts.fact: For a local/municipal race, the recommended budget split is 35-45% CTV/streaming TV and 55-65% mobile/digital.
facts.quote: **Local/municipal race:** * CTV/Streaming TV: 35-45% * Mobile/Digital: 55-65%

facts.fact: In the early campaign phase (6+ months out), the page recommends spending 60-70% on CTV.
facts.quote: **Early phase (6+ months out):** Weight toward TV for name recognition. Spend 60-70% on CTV to build baseline awareness.

facts.fact: In the mid campaign phase (3-6 months out), the page recommends shifting to a 50/50 or 55/45 TV/mobile split.
facts.quote: **Mid phase (3-6 months out):** Balance evenly. Start cross-screen retargeting sequences. Shift to 50/50 or 55/45 TV/mobile.

facts.fact: In the late campaign phase (final 8 weeks), the page recommends a 40/60 TV/mobile split.
facts.quote: **Late phase (final 8 weeks):** Shift toward mobile for action. ... Move to 40/60 TV/mobile, with mobile focused on calls to action.

facts.fact: CTV political ad disclaimers typically must be visible for a minimum of 4 seconds on most streaming platforms.
facts.quote: The disclaimer must be visible for a minimum duration (typically 4 seconds).

facts.fact: For political CTV campaigns, a completion rate above 90% is described as standard.
facts.quote: For political CTV campaigns, a completion rate above 90% is standard (TV ads are non-skippable on most platforms).

facts.fact: Click-through rates for political mobile ads typically range from 0.3% to 0.8%.
facts.quote: On mobile, click-through rates for political ads typically range from 0.3% to 0.8%

facts.fact: Donation conversion rates for political mobile ads are typically 1% to 3% for warm audiences.
facts.quote: with donation conversion rates of 1% to 3% for warm audiences.

facts.fact: Industry data cited by the page (VAB, 2024) suggests a 15% to 30% lift in key metrics when cross-screen coordination is executed well.
facts.quote: Industry data suggests a 15% to 30% lift in key metrics when cross-screen coordination is executed well (VAB, 2024).

facts.fact: A congressional district cross-screen campaign might cost $50,000 to $200,000 over a full cycle, according to the page.
facts.quote: A congressional district cross-screen campaign might run $50,000 to $200,000 over a full cycle

facts.fact: A basic cross-screen strategy for a local race could cost $5,000 to $20,000, according to the page.
facts.quote: a local race could execute a basic cross-screen strategy for $5,000 to $20,000.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its CTV ads can be run starting at $30 a day.
facts.quote: A local campaign can run CTV ads through platforms like [Adwave](https://adwave.com/how-it-works) starting at $30 a day

facts.fact: The page says campaigns report 20% to 40% higher donation conversion rates from TV-retargeted audiences versus cold mobile audiences.
facts.quote: Campaigns report 20% to 40% higher donation conversion rates from retargeted audiences versus cold mobile audiences.

facts.fact: The page recommends serving the mobile retargeting ad within 24 hours after the CTV ad for fundraising sequences.
facts.quote: In the next 24 hours, serve a mobile ad to the same households with a direct donation ask
